title: Final Fantasy XIV Got So Popular Square Enix Stopped Selling It
hook:
In December 2021 Square Enix pulled Final Fantasy XIV off the shelves for more than a month because too many people were playing it. Have you ever sat in a login queue that long?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Final Fantasy Fourteen once got so popular that Square Enix stopped selling it? In December twenty twenty one the Endwalker expansion launched, and players poured in faster than the servers could handle. Login queues stretched for hours at peak times. A bug called error two thousand two even kicked people out while they waited. Square Enix could not simply add more servers. Producer Naoki Yoshida explained that a worldwide semiconductor shortage meant the hardware for new worlds was not available. So on December fifteenth, about two weeks after Endwalker's early access began, he announced an unusual fix. Square Enix suspended sales of the Starter Edition and the Complete Edition. It also stopped taking new free trial sign ups. Every subscriber had already been given seven free days of game time. Yoshida then added fourteen more days for everyone with an active subscription. The pause lasted more than a month. Digital sales came back on January twenty fifth, twenty twenty two, with new servers on the way. Not many publishers have ever turned away paying customers because the game was too popular. Have you ever sat in a login queue that long? Follow for more gaming history.
